title: Same Symptom, Different Cause: Yellowing Leaves
summary: Practice separating a visible yellowing pattern from competing nutritional, root-zone and environmental explanations before choosing the next evidence to collect.
observedPattern: Older lower leaves are yellowing while newer growth remains comparatively greener.

hypotheses.label: Low supply or limited nutrient availability
hypotheses.whyPlausible: A tissue-age pattern can be consistent with a mobile-nutrient limitation, but the visual pattern alone is not proof.
evidenceThatRaisesConfidence: root-zone pH trend supports reduced availability
pattern progresses consistently across matched plants
evidenceThatLowersConfidence: pattern is localized to a heat or airflow anomaly

hypotheses.label: Root-zone water, aeration or salinity stress
hypotheses.whyPlausible: Root dysfunction can limit uptake even when nutrients are present in the feed.
evidenceThatRaisesConfidence: abnormal root-zone moisture or aeration history
root discoloration or reduced root vigor where visible
evidenceThatLowersConfidence: root-zone measurements are stable and matched controls share the same conditions
independent tissue/feed evidence supports a specific supply deficiency

hypotheses.label: Environmental or localized canopy stress
hypotheses.whyPlausible: Temperature, airflow, light distribution and other localized conditions can produce stress patterns that overlap with nutrient symptoms.
evidenceThatRaisesConfidence: recent setpoint/equipment change precedes the pattern
matched root-zone chemistry differs little between affected and unaffected plants
evidenceThatLowersConfidence: pattern follows tissue age across the entire crop
environmental measurements are spatially uniform while nutrition/root-zone evidence diverges

discriminatingEvidence: Record tissue age, organ position, distribution and progression before naming a cause.
Compare feed and root-zone pH/EC using consistent methods.
Review irrigation/moisture history and root condition.
Compare affected and unaffected zones for temperature, humidity, airflow and light context.
Use laboratory/tissue analysis where appropriate and authorized when the decision requires stronger evidence.
boundary: This activity teaches differential reasoning. It does not diagnose a crop, prescribe a nutrient correction, or authorize pesticide, HVAC, electrical, irrigation-system or other controlled operational changes.
